correctness.rationale: The proof defines the precise ordinary matching complex of the pentagonal prism, the full order-20 automorphism group and the ordinary geometric quotient. Exhaustive enumeration of all 32768 subsets of 15 graph edges gives 341 nonempty matching faces; all barycentric chains and 20 actions are generated, and independent Burnside checks reproduce orbit-cell counts (35,188,357,276,72). Quotient cell orientations are valid since subgroup actions preserve strict chain ranks, so there are no simplex inversions. Every boundary composition is checked exactly. The fully specified integral certificate has 463 valid +/-1 differential pivots, leaving only Z in dimensions 0 and 3, with no torsion. An independent fundamental-group certificate presents 154 generators after a 34-edge spanning tree and kills all via witnessed two-cell relators in 4 rounds (97,36,17,4); thus pi1=1. Hurewicz and homological Whitehead turn integral homology S3 plus simple connectivity into the full stated homotopy equivalence. The supplied standalone Python checker was executed from the final package and reproduced the recorded VERIFY_OK. Neither rational-only computation nor partial sampling is used.

originality.rationale: Two very close published mathematical records on this exact matching complex were read in full. One determines the original complex as S2 wedge S2 wedge S3 wedge S3 and its rational symmetry character, while the other explicitly concludes only rational cohomology of S3 for the geometric quotient and declines a homotopy claim. The present independent integral quotient-chain certificate plus a direct fundamental-group presentation is strictly stronger and is not implied by the rational characters. The 2016 anchor treats open grids; the revised 2026 nearby work treats independence and perfect-matching complexes. The line-graph formulation and exact table and aliases were explicitly searched. Priority remains contingent on potentially unindexed equivalent work.

value.rationale: The ordinary matching complex of the pentagonal prism and its full graph automorphism action are natural, not arbitrarily sliced. The quotient rationally resembling a three-sphere is documented in a specific prior mathematical record, but that alone leaves its integral torsion and fundamental group genuinely uncertain. The result determines the complete integral homotopy type of a nonfree symmetry quotient and gives two independently replayable exact certificates for the missing obstructions; this exact finite homotopy classification is mathematically useful even without a theorem for all prism lengths.
